selection_reason: recursive call -> merges nested objects -> may propagate attacker-controlled values deeper into object structure
source_summary: Function accepts arbitrary objects as parameters 'o' and 'objects' which can contain nested objects with user-controlled values
sink_summary: Recursive merge operation modifies the target object 'o' in-place, potentially affecting downstream code that uses the merged object
guard_summary: Uses 'is-plain-object' to check if both values are plain objects before recursion; null/undefined checks prevent some edge cases
risk_pattern: Recursive merge of nested objects without depth limits or prototype pollution protection may allow attacker-controlled values to deeply penetrate object structure
enclosing_conditions: if (isObject(val) && isObject(value)) - condition for recursive merge
context_summary: Library function for deep object merging that recursively copies missing properties from source objects to target object

hypotheses.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
hypotheses.fit_reason: Recursive merge of user-controlled objects without validation of keys like __proto__ can lead to prototype pollution. Stage-2 evidence shows recursive object merge with isObject check but no prototype key filtering.
Uncontrolled recursion depth in deep object merge can cause stack overflow or CPU exhaustion. Stage-2 evidence mentions missing depth limits as unresolved fact.

hypotheses.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
hypotheses.fit_reason: Prototype pollution can escalate to XSS if polluted properties are used in HTML generation. Retrieved rule links recursive merge to XSS as a potential impact.
